question: Fleming's right hand rule is used to find the direction of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Induced current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of the induced current when a conductor moves through a magnetic field.
 
• According to Fleming’s right-hand rule, if you stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular, the thumb represents the direction of motion of the conductor, the forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger represents the direction of the induced current.
 
• This rule is particularly useful in understanding the working of electric generators where mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.
 
• It helps to visualize and remember the orientation of the three quantities: magnetic field, motion, and induced current, which are orthogonal to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Induced Current:**

 
 
• When a conductor moves through a magnetic field, an electromotive force (EMF) is induced in the conductor, which in turn causes a current to flow if the circuit is closed. This current is called the induced current.
 
• Induced current is a result of electromagnetic induction, a fundamental principle of electromagnetism discovered by Michael Faraday.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the process by which a changing magnetic field within a conductor induces a current.
 
• This phenomenon is the working principle behind many electrical devices, such as transformers, inductors, and most types of electrical generators and motors.
 
 
 
• **Electric Field:**
 
 
• An electric field is a region around a charged particle where a force would be exerted on other charges.
 
• It is a vector field that represents the Coulomb force per unit charge exerted on a positive test charge at any point in space.
 
 
 
• **Potential:**
 
 
• Electrical potential, or voltage, is the potential energy per unit charge associated with a static electric field.
 
• It is the work needed to move a test charge from a reference point to a specific point inside the field without producing an acceleration.
